title: LEGION-105: stop a finished tree's root and workers at linger, keep the transcript for a reopen, and make every recovery/registration path refuse a lingering or closed tree
spec: dispatch://LEGION-105 spec version 2 (Requirements, Design, Errors, Testing rows are all covered below; the Spec-coverage table at the end maps each row to a task).
baseline: main 301bd59566fb (`chore: release pi-envoy v1.51.1`); every line number below is at this commit, the workspace @ is empty on top of it. `.legion/plan.json` and `.legion/implement.json` on main are LEGION-186's leaked handoffs (known: recorded in LEGION-31's spec); this planner's handoff overwrites plan.json, the implementer's overwrites implement.json, and the `.legion/` deletion at the end of review removes both from main.
goal: One pull request, tier T2, branch legion/LEGION-105 off main, against main, no state schema bump, no daemon API contract bump (LEGION_DAEMON_API_VERSION stays 7; packages/pi-envoy is untouched). Daemon changes only: packages/daemon/src/daemon/processes.ts, index.ts, api.ts (one interface line), api/routes/process.ts, legion-state.ts (one doc comment), AGENTS.md; tests in packages/daemon/src/daemon/__tests__/{processes,api,index,real-shutdown-e2e}.test.ts.
summaryForAPhone: When an issue finishes, Legion today only marks its tree 'lingering' and leaves the architect's process running until the linger window ends hours later; meanwhile three recovery paths treat that tree as alive and wake or relaunch it. This plan makes linger stop the processes right away (keeping the architect's transcript so a reopen resumes it), teaches the sweep and boot to clean up what is left, and makes every wake, relaunch, and registration path refuse a finished tree.
globalConstraints: Spec Requirements row 9: no state schema change. TreeState/WorkerRoleClaim fields are unchanged; `resumeSessionFile` (already optional, v30) is simply populated at linger and deleted at close.

No daemon API contract bump: nothing on the wire changes shape. New 409 refusals on /process/started and /process/ready reuse `HttpError(409, message)`; the pi-envoy extension already exits on a 4xx at /process/started (`exitOnRegistrationRefusal`, packages/pi-envoy/extensions/legion.ts:66-75) and at boot-time /process/ready (the `bootstrapRoot` catch at :667-681 exits on any non-retried error; `callReadyWithRetry` :109-132 retries only 5xx/network). A heartbeat-regain /process/ready 409 (`rerunReadyAfterRegain` :506-520) is logged and the process stays alive — the linger sweep retires it (spec Errors row 4 settled: no plugin change).
The stop at linger is never awaited inside `beginLinger` (durable lane, a throw there is fatal: events.ts `fatal`). `beginLinger` persists first, then starts the retire with `void …catch(log)`.

Never touch, restart, or kill the live daemon (`legion-sjawharlegion`, port 13370) or any pane you did not start. The unit suites spawn nothing real; the LEGION_E2E test uses its own `tmux -L legion-realshutdown` server and kills only that. The scratch daemon (Task 6) uses its own team slug, state dir, ports, NATS container, and tmux socket.

Never jj undo / op restore / abandon; never bun add / mise install against the live profile. `bun install --frozen-lockfile` inside the workspace is fine. Run `bunx tsc --noEmit` in packages/daemon and `bunx biome check packages/daemon/` once at the end of Task 5, never per step.
Run only the touched test files/titles during tasks (`bun test <file> -t "<title>"`); the whole `bun test packages/daemon` once at the end of Task 5.

Rebase only if GitHub reports CONFLICTING (Sami 2026-09-11). Commit with `jj -R "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" split -m "<message>" <paths>`; the implementer alone sets and pushes `legion/LEGION-105` and opens the PR with `Dispatch: LEGION-105` in the body, in the READY format from the legion-worker skill.

decisionsSettled: Factoring: one private primitive `retireTreeProcessesLocked(treeKey)` holds the root leg, the worker fixed-point loop, the locator-less claim deletion, `pruneQueueForTree`, the `spawnCapabilities` deletion, `clearTreePhases`, and the persist — everything `closeTreeLocked` does today except the status/lingerUntil writes, `removeTreeWorkspaces`, the `done` write, the slot release, and `promoteWorkerQueue`. It moves the root's `ompSessionFile` into `tree.resumeSessionFile` before deleting the locator. It throws `StopFailed` after persisting when any process would not stop (that process's locator and claim kept). Three callers: `closeTreeLocked` (inline, then the close), the public deduped `retireTreeProcesses(treeKey)` (used by `beginLinger` in the background, by `reportRootExit`'s not-closing branch, and by `retireLingeringTrees`), and `retireLingeringTrees()` (the sweep/boot pass).

`closingTrees` becomes `Map<IssueKey, { kind: "retire" | "close"; settled: Promise<void> }>`. Every `.has` reader (spawnWorker, workerReady, isTreeGone, reportRootExit/recordRootExit, retireUnconfirmedBoot, awaitClosingTrees) keeps its meaning: 'a teardown of this tree's processes is in flight'. `retireTreeProcesses` joins any in-flight entry and returns. `closeTree` loops: joins an in-flight entry; if it was a `close`, returns; if it was a `retire`, re-checks and proceeds to close — so `expireLinger` right after `beginLinger` still closes (processes.test.ts:4182 depends on this).
Secrets: nothing new. `persist()` → `pruneWrittenSecretFiles` reaps the root's boot-token/grant/envoy files once the locator is gone, exactly as at close.

Capabilities: `revokeRoleClaim` at the root leg and for every deleted claim (as `closeTreeLocked` does today); the tree's `spawnCapabilities` are deleted in the primitive (moved from close; a `todo` re-admission mints a fresh one in `spawnTree`).

`stoppingForRelaunch` is NOT used by the retire: the root's graceful stop makes it POST /process/exit; that route must send a lingering tree's root to `reportRootExit` whatever the issue status (today `backlog`/`icebox` lingers go to `markProcessDead` and would set the tree `dead`). With the retire registered in `closingTrees`, `reportRootExit` records the exit (no locator clear, slot no-op, persist) and starts nothing — no deadlock, no second close.

`reportRootExit`'s not-closing branch starts `retireTreeProcesses` instead of `closeTree({stopRoot:false})`: a root exiting on its own on a done issue no longer closes the tree at once; the tree stays lingering until `lingerUntil` and the reopen window is kept. `stopRoot` and the `options` parameter go away (`recordRootExit` already cleared the locator, so the primitive's root leg has nothing to stop). `recordRootExit` keeps `resumeSessionFile` whenever the locator carries one (close deletes it, so a re-admitted closed issue still starts fresh).

`isTreeGone` also treats `lingering` as gone: no launch, `/worker/started`, `/process/started` claim write, or late-start commit lands on a lingering tree, matching the invariant 'only the sweep and a todo re-admission touch it'. `decideWorkerRelaunch`'s `|| status === "lingering"` (:1840) becomes redundant and is removed.

`resurrectDeadTree` refuses every status but `active` and `dead` (spec Design): `queued` keeps its existing message; `lingering`/`closed`/`launch-failed` get one new line. Guard lives in `resurrectDeadTree` (the single place both `resurrect` and the held replay reach). `handleException` returns after one line for any role whose tree is lingering or closed, before the probe, the ledger claim, or the resend. The registration-deadline retry, `reconnectRoots`, and the resync probe already skip non-active trees (cited above); they are not changed and their existing tests are the locks.

Routes: `/process/started` 409s a non-active tree right after the boot-token lookup and before `boot.sessionId = rootSessionId`, so the token is unconsumed and nothing is written; the redundant `treeState.status = "active"` write goes. `/process/ready` 409s after the generation check, before `confirmRootReady`/save/`onTreeReady`/`markTreeReady`. `/process/exit` sends a `lingering` or `closed` tree's root to `reportRootExit`.
`emitOverseerCatchup` returns with one line for a non-active tree (defensive: `/process/ready`'s 409 already prevents the call; no dedicated unit test — the reviewer reads it).

Boot: `await processManager.retireLingeringTrees()` right after `reconnectWorkers` (both awaited, both before the launch hold and `enableLaunches()`): `api` is assigned (:686) so every `revokeRoleClaim` has it; `runningWorkerCount()` (worker-admission.ts:300-312) counts every claim with a locator, so the 207 lingering claims must be gone before promotion decides. Bounded by `treeStopTimeoutSeconds` per tree (trees in parallel). Boot does NOT close expired lingers — the first tick does, as today (keeps the LEGION-163 test's shape and avoids N jj workspace removals inside boot).

Sweep tick: expire first (unchanged `expireLinger` loop), then `void retireLingeringTrees()` for every lingering tree that still records a locator or a claim; an expired tree with processes gets one teardown (the retire joins the in-flight close). One log line per retired tree, one per failure.

Log wording: the root/worker stop-failure lines change from `… while closing ${treeKey}` to `… while retiring the processes of ${treeKey}` because the primitive also runs at linger; processes.test.ts:4604-4607 (`stringContaining("root process failed to stop while closing …")`) is updated to the new wording (grep `failed to stop while closing` for any other pin).

The pi-envoy extension is untouched (see globalConstraints[1]). The spec's 'planner checks how the extension's bounded ready retry treats a 409' is settled: exit at boot, stay-alive-then-swept on a regain.

steps.step: 3. Rewrite the AGENTS.md invariant paragraph (:66) — plain English, then the mechanics
steps.code: - A tree that leaves `active` for `lingering` (its issue set `done`, `backlog`, or `icebox`) loses its processes at once, not at the end of the linger window (LEGION-105). `beginLinger` records the linger (status, `lingerUntil`, the released admission slot) and persists, then — outside the durable lane, never awaited there — `retireTreeProcesses` stops the root and every worker exactly as a close does (a `{type:"shutdown"}` frame over each process's own shim socket, the pane killed directly only if it does not exit within `tree_stop_timeout_seconds`, or at once when its shim is unreachable or the process is confirmed gone; never when the pane no longer runs the recorded process, where the kill is refused and the locator clears as if gone; and never when the pane cannot be verified either way — a `list-panes` that proves nothing makes the stop throw and the locator stays), clears each locator, deletes every role claim on the tree and revokes its capability, prunes the tree's spawn capabilities and pane secret files, and keeps the root's transcript path as `TreeState.resumeSessionFile`, so a human moving the issue back to `todo` inside the window resumes the same architect (`spawnRoot` resumes whenever that field is set). A process that will not stop keeps its locator and claim and is logged once; the tree keeps its `lingerUntil`. The linger sweep (every `LINGER_SWEEP_INTERVAL_MS`) runs the same retire for every lingering tree that still records a locator or a role claim (`retireLingeringTrees`, one log line per tree) and closes each tree whose `lingerUntil` has passed (`expireLinger` → `closeTree`: the retire again, then workspaces removed, status `closed`, `lingerUntil` and `resumeSessionFile` dropped, the issue written `done` unless it already is `done`/`backlog`/`icebox`); the same retire pass runs once at boot, after `reconnectWorkers` and before `enableLaunches()`, so resident roots of finished trees are gone before any promotion decision counts their claims. Exactly two paths change a lingering tree's record: that sweep, and the issue's `todo` transition, which re-admits it. Every other path refuses: `resurrectDeadTree` (any status but `active`/`dead`), `handleException` for every reason and every role on the tree (one line, before any probe or re-send), the registration-deadline retry (`treeStillUnconfirmed`), `reconnectRoots`, and the resync probe skip it; `/process/started` and `/process/ready` answer 409 naming the tree and its status with nothing written and the boot token unconsumed (the extension exits on the started 409 and on a boot-time ready 409; a heartbeat-regain ready 409 is logged and the process waits for the sweep); the overseer catch-up is published only for an `active` tree; `isTreeGone` treats `lingering` like `closed`, so no launch, `/worker/started`, or late-start commit lands on it; a root's own `/process/exit` on a lingering (or closed) tree goes to `reportRootExit` whatever the issue's status — it records the exit, keeps the session file, joins nothing (the retire that asked it to stop already holds `closingTrees`), and never enters the dead path. The linger sweep also removes session windows not recorded by a tree or controller.
steps.notes: Then: :69 → `resumeSessionFile is cleared by a fresh locator, terminal failure, and close; linger keeps it`. :85 → `closeTree` and `retireTreeProcesses` track in-flight teardown in memory (`closingTrees`, tagged `retire`/`close`); a `closeTree` that finds a retire in flight joins it and then closes. HTTP table: `/process/started` row adds `A tree that is not active answers 409 naming the tree and status, before the token is consumed`; `/process/exit` row adds `a lingering or closed tree's root records its exit only (`reportRootExit`) whatever the issue status`. Files table: `index.ts` row adds `the linger sweep (expire, then retire)`; `processes.ts` row adds `retireTreeProcesses`/`retireLingeringTrees`. Keep each sentence true to the code the reviewer will read (Acceptance 4).
